question.problem:
Suppose that $f(x,y,z)$ is a differentiable function such that

$$
f(1,2,3)=6,\,{f}_{x}(1,2,3)=6,\,{f}_{y}(1,2,3)=3,\,{f}_{z}(1,2,3)=2.
$$

Using a linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(1,2,3)$ estimate the value of $f(1.08,1.93,3.05)$
question.worked_solution:
The linear approximation of the function $f$ at the point $(a,b,c)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y,z)≈f(a,b,c)+∇f(a,b,c)\cdot ⟨x-a,y-b,z-c⟩.
$$

So, the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(1,2,3)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & ≈f(1,2,3)+∇f(1,2,3)\cdot ⟨x-1,y-2,z-3⟩ \\  & =6+⟨{f}_{x}(1,2,3),{f}_{y}(1,2,3),{f}_{z}(1,2,3)⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,y-2,z-3⟩ \\  & =6+⟨6,3,2⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,y-2,z-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We can approximate $f(1.08,1.93,3.05)$ by evaluating the linear approximation at $x=1.08,$ $y=1.93,$ and $z=3.05$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1.08,1.93,3.05) & ≈6+⟨6,3,2⟩\cdot ⟨1.08-1,1.93-2,3.05-3⟩ \\  & =6+⟨6,3,2⟩\cdot ⟨0.08,-0.07,0.05⟩ \\  & =6+6(0.08)+3(-0.07)+2(0.05) \\  & =6+0.48-0.21+0.1 \\  & =6.37\end{aligned}
$$
